Published online:
September 3, 2026

Geographic focus:
Global (primary focus: Japan/USD-JPY FX dynamics, US monetary policy, with secondary mentions of NZ, Canada, UK, Eurozone)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references July 31 intervention, recent BOJ/Fed speeches
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Friday NFP, September Fed hike, BOJ hike this month
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
The yen surged ~1.5% to 156.36/USD, driven by hawkish BOJ commentary from board member Takata pushing for expedited rate hikes to counter inflation — not government intervention. Markets have near-fully priced a BOJ hike this month. On the US side, Fed Chair Warsh's recent hawkish speech has markets pricing a 61% chance of a September Fed hike, complicating a sustained USD/JPY downtrend. Friday's NFP (consensus: +56K, after prior -23K shock) is the next key catalyst. A solid print would reinforce Fed hike bets; only a significantly weak number would materially reduce September hike odds.
